article.headline: Chevron Edges Up 1% With $7 Billion Venezuela Bet In Focus
article.deck: Chevron is back on its 50-day line and inside the buy range of a flat base, 0.4% past the 217.88 buy point with room up to 228.77.
body: Chevron rose 2.36 to 218.71, up 1.1%, as of 1:30 p.m. Mountain, bouncing off its 50-day line. The stock broke out Oct. 14 from a four-week flat base 7.8% deep with a 217.88 buy point; that session traded 1.12x its 50-day average volume. The base topped Sept. 15 and bottomed Sept. 22. Today's price sits 0.4% above the buy point and inside the buy range, which runs to 228.77. The session is on pace for 0.39x its 50-day average volume.

It has been 22 sessions since the breakout, and the stock has given back most of the run: it trades 7.5% below its 52-week high of 236.48. The 50-day line sits at 215.46, 1.5% below the price, and the 200-day at 195.79. The stock is exactly on its 21-day line at 218.73, 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line, so the trend is neither stretched nor broken. Chevron holds RS rank 77 of 99 on the desk's list; its RS line sits 12.8% below its high. The stock is up 43.5% this year and 42.7% over 12 months.

The September quarter brought EPS of 5.06, up 178%, on revenue of $65.24 billion, up 35.4%. The June quarter earned 6.11 a share on $67.20 billion in revenue, after 1.11 on $47.56 billion in March and 1.39 on $45.79 billion in the December 2025 quarter. Market value is $426.8 billion at 13.26 times forward earnings. The next report is due Jan. 29.
24/7 Wall St. ran a piece Friday headlined "Chevron Bets $7B on Venezuela While Exxon Mobil Plays It Safe."
A close back under the 50-day line would turn this from a bounce into a stalled breakout.
article.watch: Whether Chevron holds the 215.46 50-day line and the 217.88 buy point into the close.

article.headline: Zeta Global Slips 2% But Holds Gains As Revenue Climbs 46%
article.deck: Three sessions after clearing a 34.90 cup buy point, Zeta sits 4.9% past it, at the top edge of a buy range that ends at 36.65.
body: Zeta Global fell 0.65 to 36.62, down 1.8%, as of 1:30 p.m. Mountain, on pace for 0.82x its 50-day average volume. The stock broke out Nov. 10 from a five-week cup 15.6% deep with a 34.90 buy point; the breakout session traded 1.92x its 50-day average. The cup's left side peaked Oct. 5 and the low came Nov. 5. Today's price is 4.9% above the buy point, three cents under the 36.65 top of the buy range.

The stock trades 5.6% below its 52-week high of 38.80. It is 1.46 ATRs from the 21-day line at 33.48, an intact trend rather than a stretched one, and 13.9% above its 50-day line at 32.14. Zeta holds RS rank 99 of 99 on the desk's list, and its RS line sits 2.1% from its high. Shares are up 79.9% this year and 78.9% over 12 months.

Revenue in the September quarter reached $492.7 million, up 46.1%, with EPS of 0.14. Sales have stepped up every quarter in the table: $394.6 million in the December 2025 quarter, $396.3 million in March and $442.8 million in June. EPS went from 0.03 to a 0.06 loss, then 0.03 and 0.14. The desk's calendar had the company's earnings date on Nov. 9, the session before the breakout. Market value is $9.35 billion at 27.18 times forward earnings.
Zacks ran pieces headlined "ZETA Gains 17% in the Past Month as AI Growth & Margins Accelerate" and "3 Top-Ranked AI Stocks Holding Up Despite the Selloff."
A move past 36.65 takes the stock out of the buy range; a slide back under 34.90 would make it a stalled breakout.
article.watch: The 36.65 top of the buy range above and the 34.90 buy point below.

article.headline: Costco Rises 1% Near Record Amid $4 Billion Buyback, Special Dividend
article.deck: Costco is clearing a 25-week cup at a 1,096.60 buy point today, 0.7% past it with a buy range up to 1,151.43.
body: Costco rose 12.21 to 1,104.42, up 1.1%, as of 1:30 p.m. Mountain, breaking out of a 25-week cup. The base ran from a May 19 peak to a Sept. 25 low and corrected 19.5%. The buy point is 1,096.60, and the price sits 0.7% above it, inside a buy range that runs to 1,151.43. The session is on pace for 0.57x its 50-day average volume.

The stock trades 0.5% below its 52-week high of 1,109.50. The run into the breakout has been steep: it is 2.95 ATRs from the 21-day line at 1,034.85, just under the 3-ATR mark where a move reads as stretched, and 14.2% above its 50-day line at 967.08. Costco holds RS rank 83 of 99 on the desk's list; the RS line sits 6.9% below its high. Shares are up 12.9% in a month, 28.1% this year and 20.8% over 12 months.

The August quarter delivered EPS of 6.75, up 15%, on revenue of $95.72 billion, up 11.1%. The three quarters before it earned 4.50 on $67.31 billion, 4.58 on $69.60 billion and 4.93 on $70.53 billion. The next report is due Dec. 10. Market value is $489.5 billion at 44.12 times forward earnings.
Zacks ran a piece Friday headlined "Costco Hits All-Time High Amid $4 Billion Buyback, Special Dividend," and another asking whether the special dividend is reason enough to own the stock.
A close back under 1,096.60 would leave the breakout stalled on day one.
article.watch: Whether Costco closes above the 1,096.60 buy point and takes out the 1,109.50 high.
